1. ACCOMMODATION:
(i) Lord President and Chief Justices—

Free fully furnished institutional quarters, one butler, two
gardeners, one caretaker and a provision of $1,000 per annum
for house and grounds upkeep shall be provided:

Provided that where the Lord President or a Chief Justice
has been granted a government housing loan referred to in
paragraph 11, the continued occupation of the said institu-
tional quarters shall be subject to a rental of 20% of his
salary or 20 times the nominal rent whichever is the lesser.

(ii) Judges of the Federal Court and the High Courts—

Institutional quarters may be provided subject to a rental
at 10% of salary or 10 times the nominal rent whichever is
the lesser:

Provided that where a Judge has been granted a govern-
ment housing loan referred to in paragraph 11, the continued
occupation of the said institutional quarters shall be subject
to a rental of 20% of his salary or 20 times the nominal rent
whichever is the lesser.

3. OFFICIAL CAR:

(i) Lord President and Chief Justices—

A Government car not exceeding $20,000 in value inclusive
of cost of accessories shall be provided with syce. Main-
tenance, petrol, oil and lubrication shall be borne by
Government.

(ii) Judges of the Federal Court and the High Courts—

A Government car not exceeding $14,000 in value inclusive
of cost of accessories shall be provided. Maintenance of the
car shall be borne by Government. Petrol, oil and lubrication
shall be borne by the Judge.

6. SUBSISTENCE ALLOWANCE:
   When on duty exceeding 8 hours away from station—$20

per day.

7. LODGING EXPENSES:
Actual expenses supported by receipts shall be reimbursed.

8. MEDICAL FACILITIES:

Free medical treatment for Judges, their wives and children but,
in case of hospitalisation, the Judge shall pay ward daily charges
at the rate of $8 per person. A Judge shall be entitled to receive
free of charge such medicines, medical assistance and attendance
as Government has at its disposal, including artificial limbs and
orthopaedic appliances.

9. LEAVE:
(i) Vacation Leave—

At the rate of 30 days in a year excluding public holidays
and weekly holidays. Vacation leave shall be taken in the
year in which it accrues and where, owing to exigencies of
the service, it has not been taken in the current year, it can
be carried forward into the succeeding year. Vacation leave
in respect of any three consecutive years may be accumulated
for the purpose of overseas travel and such accumulation and
oveseas travel shall be subject to prior approval. Approving
authority for the purpose of this section shall be—

(a) in the case of the Lord President, the Prime Minister;

(b) in the case of the Chief Justices and the Federal Judges,

the Lord President;

(c) in the case of other Judges, the Chief Justices concerned.

(ii) Medical Leave—

Sick leave up to 90 days at one time or up to a maximum
of 90 days in any one year (January to December). But
additional medical leave of not more than 90 days may be
given with the approval of the Prime Minister in the case of
the Lord President and of the Lord President in the case of

other Judges.

(2nd Schedule]

(iii) Tuberculosis Leave—

Up to a maximum of 12 months on full pay. Thereafter,
6 months half-pay and further 6 months without pay.

10. DEATH AND INJURY BENEFITS IN AIRCRAFT ACCIDENTS:

Liabilities for an injury or death arising out of an aircraft
accident in the course of duty shall be borne entirely by the
Government. The rates of death and disablement benefits for
Judges arising from such accidents shall be as follows—

(a) For death caused by an injury sustained in an accident, a sum
of $150,000:

Provided that where the dependants or legal personal
representatives are entitled to receive similar benefits under
any other provisions of this Act, such dependants or legal
personal representatives shall be entitled at their option to
receive one benefit only.

(b) For permanent disablement caused by an injury sustained in
an accident resulting in—

(i) loss of two or more limbs by actual separation at or
above the wrist or ankle; or the total and irrecoverable
loss of all sight of both eyes; or the loss of one limb
accompanied by the loss of sight of one eye: $275,000.

(ii) loss of one limb by actual separation at or above the
wrist or ankle; or the total and irrecoverable loss of
sight of one eye: $150,000.

(iii) total incapacity (total disablement) from engaging in or
giving attention to any profession or occupation:
$275,000.

(iv) partial disablement: proportionate, according to medical
assessment of the percentage degree of such disablement.

11. HousinG LOAN SCHEME:

The Housing Loan Scheme as is applicable to members of the
Public Service.
